sources: IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.9 — Buildings sector has 67% potential reduction in final energy demand before additional electrification
IPCC AR6 SYR Section 4.5.3 — Integrated building design offers growing examples of zero-energy or zero-carbon buildings across regions
IEA Global Heat Pump Report 2023 — Heat pumps reduce heating emissions 40–80% vs gas boilers depending on grid mix
IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.9 — Buildings mitigation potential reaches 2.5–3 GtCO2eq/yr by 2030 at costs below $100/tCO2

planetary_limits.note: Reduced cooling demand lowers water use in cooling towers

societal_indicators.note: Renovated buildings reduce energy bills 40–60% for low-income households
Construction is non-delocalisable; EU estimates 160 000 additional jobs per doubling of renovation rate

interactions.note: Heat pumps deliver full decarbonisation benefit only when powered by clean electricity
Carbon price accelerates investment in deep renovation by raising heating fuel costs

methodological_note: Median impact of 2.5 GtCO2/yr calibrated against IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.9 which identifies 1.5–3 GtCO2eq/yr potential in buildings at <$100/tCO2. Slow ramp (full effect year 2045) reflects building stock inertia (50–80 year lifetime). Pessimistic scenario accounts for rebound effect (lower energy costs encouraging more consumption) and slower adoption in developing-nation construction boom. Projection baseline: SSP2-4.5.
